basic: Two tiles already known to be in different pieces have a wall between them.
size: Two groups that are too big together get a wall between them.
grow: A group that is still too small grows through its only way out.
min-grow: A group below the Minimum grows through its only way out.
reach: A group joins the tiles it needs to reach an allowed size.
min-reach: A group joins the tiles it needs to reach the Minimum.
rose-grow: A group that still misses a rose type grows through its only way out.
rose-reach: A group goes the only way that leads to a rose it still misses.
rose-pair: Two roses of the same type are in different pieces.
rose-cut: When roses are behind a narrow passage, each passage tile leads one piece to its roses.
rose-region: A closed-in area with one rose of each type is one piece.
stamp-place: Edges outside every place the polyomino's shape fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.
stamp-size: A polyomino's piece is never bigger than its shape.
stamp-shape: A polyomino's piece never leaves its shape.
stamp-pair: Two polyominoes of the same shape that one shape cannot cover are in different pieces.
shape-fit: A group has to stay inside the polyomino's shape.
bank-fit: A group has to stay inside one of the bank shapes.
ban-fit: A group never becomes a shape of the Omits.
bank-place: Edges outside every place a bank shape fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.
bank-region: A closed-in area can be cut into bank shapes in only one way.
bank-bend: Every bank shape has a bend, so every piece gets one.
bank-block: Every bank shape holds a 2x2 block, so every piece gets one.
bridge-count: At a single connection between two sides, only one choice leaves each side a number of tiles that whole pieces can cover.
area-sum: When the area numbers add up to every tile, each tile joins a numbered piece.
area-region: The area numbers of a closed-in area fit in it in only one way.
area-place: Every place the numbered piece can take agrees on this edge.
area-rel: A wall that compares sizes leaves only some sizes for the pieces on its two sides.
range-count: Only some sizes can still fill the whole board, and these two groups together would have none of them.
range-region: A closed-in area is cut into whole pieces of the allowed sizes in only one way.
euler-count: When only a few pieces are allowed, there are only so many walls.
colour-count: When only a few pieces are allowed, groups that cannot be different pieces are the same piece.
match-iso: With Match, a wall inside one piece has its copy in every other piece.
match-place: With Match, edges outside every place the one shape fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.
match-region: With Match, a closed-in area with the size of one piece is one piece.
match-fit: With Match, one shape has to fit every group.
match-size: With Match, only some sizes can fill the whole board.
match-mismatch: Match and Mismatch together leave one single piece.
mismatch-place: With Mismatch, a group that can only become one shape follows the places that shape fits.
mismatch-stamp: With Mismatch, two polyominoes of the same shape are in one piece.
mismatch-link: With Mismatch, two groups that can only become the same shape are one piece.
mismatch-hall: With Mismatch, pieces that can only be a few shapes take them all, and the others lose those shapes.
mismatch-count: With Mismatch, each size has only so many shapes, so only some sizes can fill the board.
mingle-area-link: With Size Separation, two neighbours that must have the same size are one piece.
mingle-shape-link: With Mingle Shape, two neighbours that must have the same shape are one piece.
mingle-area-merge: With Size Separation, groups that end with different sizes are different pieces.
mingle-shape-merge: With Mingle Shape, groups that end with different shapes are different pieces.
mingle-area-parity: With Size Separation and only two sizes, the sizes alternate across every wall.
mingle-shape-parity: With Mingle Shape and only two shapes, the shapes alternate across every wall.
mingle-area-place: With Size Separation, a piece of known size only goes where it touches no piece of that size.
mingle-area-single: With Size Separation and only one size possible, no two pieces can touch: the board is one piece.
mingle-shape-single: With Mingle Shape and only one shape possible, no two pieces can touch: the board is one piece.
mingle-area-corner: With Size Separation and only two sizes, three pieces never meet at a corner.
mingle-shape-corner: With Mingle Shape and only two shapes, three pieces never meet at a corner.
solitude-grow: With Solitude, a group without a symbol grows through its only way out.
solitude-reach: With Solitude, a group goes the only way that leads to a symbol.
solitude-pair: With Solitude, two symbols are in different pieces.
solitude-region: With Solitude, a closed-in area with one symbol is one piece.
boxy-place: With Boxy, edges outside every rectangle that fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.
boxy-line: With Boxy, a piece with a prime number of tiles is a straight strip.
boxy-corner: With Boxy, walls never bend at a corner.
boxy-fill: With Boxy, a piece fills the smallest rectangle around its tiles.
nonbox-grow: With Non-boxy, a group that is still a rectangle grows through its only way out.
pal-wall: A palisade gets exactly its number of walls: this side has to be one.
pal-link: A palisade gets exactly its number of walls: this side has to stay open.
pal-pair: Two palisades side by side share a side, which counts for both.
pal-two: When only two pieces can exist, every wall has the same two pieces on its sides.
pal-size: A palisade's open sides give its piece a smallest size.
wally-wall: With Wally, a tile never has three neighbours in its piece.
wally-link: With Wally, a tile keeps at most two neighbours in its piece, and here only one way is left.
wally-ends: With Wally, a piece is a path with two ends.
wally-line: With Wally, the two pieces of a Gemini wall have lines of the same length.
wally-two: With Wally and only two pieces, every wall has the same two pieces on its sides.
gemini-line: The two pieces of a Gemini wall have lines of the same length.
gemini-anchor: Across a Gemini wall, a finished line in one piece has to match the only line the other piece has room for.
gemini-place: Across a Gemini wall both sides keep the shapes they share; across a Delta wall they cannot end the same.
gd-clash: A Gemini wall and a Delta wall are never between the same two pieces.
bri-three: With Bricky, four walls never meet at a corner: after three, the fourth edge is open.
bri-pinch: With Bricky, two tiles of one piece that touch at a corner are joined through a third tile.
bri-vertex: With Bricky, every way to split the four tiles around a corner agrees on this edge.
loo-outline: With Loopy, no wall touches the outline.
loo-three: With Loopy, an even number of walls meets at every corner: after three, the fourth edge is a wall.
loo-corner: With Loopy, at a corner where a hole pokes in, the two other edges are both walls or both open.
loo-color: With Loopy, a wall changes the colour of a tile and an open edge keeps it.
tower-wall: A watchtower counts the pieces around its corner: here the tiles have to be apart.
tower-link: A watchtower counts the pieces around its corner: here the tiles have to be together.
tower-wrap: A piece never wraps around a watchtower corner.
compass: A compass piece goes the only way that gives it enough tiles on that side.
cmp-block: A tile out of the compass piece's reach is cut off by a wall.
cmp-budget: A compass number is exact, so the piece has only so many tiles to spend on its way to a rose.
cmp-wrap: The compass piece needs this tile to have enough tiles on one side.
cmp-place: Tiles in every piece that fits the compass are joined, tiles in none of them are cut off.
cmp-crowd: Several compasses share the tiles, and only one choice leaves enough for each.
cmp-excl: A tile that breaks the compass numbers stays out of the piece.
cmp-box: With Boxy, a compass counts whole rows or columns of its rectangle.
diff-clash: A piece with two Difference walls of different numbers has two different neighbours.
diff-small: With Mismatch and a Maximum, Difference walls need small pieces, and there are only a few.
rose-cover: Every way to share the roses between pieces keeps these two groups apart.
label: Every tile belongs to the piece of one clue, and here only one clue is left for it.
box-hall: With Boxy and Mismatch, pieces that can only be a few rectangles take them all.
box-all: With Boxy and Mismatch, when the board needs every rectangle left, each is used once.
region-merge: In a closed-in area, the sizes the walls ask for fit only with these groups as one piece.
size-cut: When every piece has the same size, the tiles behind one narrow tile have to make whole pieces.
hetero-size: With Heterogeneous, a size is used only once.
hetero-link: With Heterogeneous, two neighbours that must have the same size are one piece.
hetero-merge: With Heterogeneous, groups that end with different sizes are different pieces.
hetero-parity: With Heterogeneous and only two sizes, the sizes alternate across every wall.
hetero-place: With Heterogeneous, a piece of known size only goes where it touches no piece of that size.
hetero-single: With Heterogeneous and only one size possible, no two pieces can touch: the board is one piece.
hetero-corner: With Heterogeneous and only two sizes, three pieces never meet at a corner.
clue-apart: Two clues that cannot be in one piece get a wall between their groups.
pair-apart: Two groups that cannot be one piece get a wall between them.
fact:far-join: Tiles that are far apart can be known to be in one piece before the way between them is known.
fact:label-join: Tiles that can only belong to the same clue are one piece, even far apart.
fact:clue-join: Two clues that cannot be in different pieces are in one piece.
fact:pair-join: Two groups that cannot be different pieces are one piece.
fact:split-cut: When only one way connects two tiles of a piece, that way is part of the piece.
